intel_scenarios.title: Planning scenarios
intel_scenarios.subtitle: Try a change on a model of the plant before it touches the schedule: what-ifs, optimised sequences, their cost and their trade-offs.
intel_scenarios.how: A scenario is simulated on the same baseline the scheduler uses and changes nothing live. Applying it needs somebody else's approval and runs through the scheduler; the schedule it replaces is kept so it can be put back.
intel_scenarios.name: Name
intel_scenarios.description: What is being tried, and why
intel_scenarios.seed_hint: Same input and seed, same answer
intel_scenarios.objectives_hint: How much each objective matters. The score weighs every change from the baseline by these, and conflicts between them are spelled out.
intel_scenarios.changes_hint: Assumptions are conditions of the world and are only simulated. Levers (order changes) are decisions and are what applying pushes to the scheduler.
intel_scenarios.stale: Production orders have changed since this was simulated. Simulate it again before it is approved or applied.
intel_scenarios.four_eyes: You built or proposed this scenario; somebody else approves it.
intel_scenarios.compare_hint: Baseline: the plant as scheduled today with the {rule} rule.
intel_scenarios.bottleneck_hint: Centres at 85% or more are bottlenecks.
intel_scenarios.score_hint: Weighted change from the baseline by your priorities; negative is better.
intel_scenarios.no_change: No measurable change from the baseline.
intel_scenarios.tensions: Priorities that pull against each other
intel_scenarios.plan_hint: Only these reach the live schedule, through the scheduler.
intel_scenarios.no_order_changes: No order changes: the scheduler is re-run with this rule.
intel_scenarios.no_assumptions: None: the plant as it is.
intel_scenarios.no_matrix: No changeovers are recorded, so every job pays its routing setup, as in the scheduler.
intel_scenarios.actual_summary: {done} order(s) finished, {open} still open. Mean finish error {mae} day(s). On time: {on} actual against {pred} predicted.

note.rollback: Why the previous schedule is put back

k.queue_waits: Operations held by a queue limit

changeovers.title: Changeover matrix
changeovers.subtitle: Setup time from one product or family to the next, by work centre. The digital twin and the optimiser sequence by it.
changeovers.empty: No changeovers recorded: every job pays its routing setup.
changeovers.precedence: The most specific rule wins: a centre's own rule over an every-centre rule, a product over its family, a family over anything. The same product again needs no changeover; with no rule, the routing's setup stands.

twin.title: Digital twin
twin.subtitle: The plant as the scenarios see it: factories, lines, work centres, their capacity, load, queues and resource use. Read from live records, never written back.
twin.capacity: {m} min a day · {j} job(s) at once

intel_scenarios.suggested_hint: Open external disruptions turned into what-if changes. Nothing is added until you choose it; check the figures before simulating.
